candidates.tagline: The 'no more keys' smart lock that needs a hand crank when the battery dies
candidates.story: Ring's first smart lock ($249) solves the dead-battery lockout problem with a built-in power dial — turn it a few times and the crank generator gives the electronics just enough power to accept your PIN; founder Jamie Siminoff pitched the lock as the end of 'little pieces of metal in our pockets', but the backup when digital fails is manual cranking.
candidates.why_funny: The inventor's argument against physical keys is that they're primitive, yet his solution when the smart lock's battery dies is turning a hand crank like you're starting a 1920s motorcar.
candidates.alt: Black Ring Smart Lock mounted on a wooden door, showing a stacked fingerprint reader and backlit keypad with the knurled power-generating dial below them

candidates.tagline: Car makers spent a decade removing every button — China just ordered them all back
candidates.story: China's MIIT published draft regulations on October 10, 2026 requiring physical switches alongside touchscreens for headlights, wipers, defrosters, and gear selection in all vehicles — after automakers spent billions engineering interiors with zero physical controls to look futuristic.
candidates.why_funny: The entire design language of the modern luxury EV — one giant screen, no buttons anywhere — just got officially classified as a design flaw by the world's largest car market.
candidates.alt: The centrally-mounted 15.4-inch touchscreen of a Tesla Model 3, showing the car's minimalist interior with no physical buttons on the dashboard — exactly the interface China is now requiring physical controls alongside
